findings.text: Filter entry arbitrates whether a BPF program may call a scheduler extension helper. It receives the program descriptor plus a helper identity, classifies the helper into usage families, then permits or denies the reference based on program flavor and attachment context.

Non scheduler helpers are always permitted. System call programs may use only helpers marked for unlocked contexts, processor selection, idle inspection, universal use or compartment identity, while other program flavors outside structure operations are limited to universal, idle and compartment families. Structure operation programs without an attached operations table are temporarily permitted to allow collection before attachment validation.

Structure operation programs attached to foreign operations tables are denied. Programs attached to the compartment oriented table are denied processor only helpers to prevent confusion between small signed processor and compartment values, whereas the reverse direction remains permissive to ease migration. Remaining helpers are authorized through a per operation permission table indexed from the attachment offset.
Operation slot indices derive from byte offsets scaled by the size of a generic operation pointer, applied both to member offsets and to scheduler operation fields.

Boot initialization validates shared layout equivalence between processor and compartment operation forms, registers helper sets for multiple program flavors, initializes idle tracking and compartment helpers, registers both operation flavors, attaches power management notification, creates kernel object hierarchy with global attributes, and fails with diagnostic on any step failure.

Processor and compartment operation structures must share identical offsets for common data, shared callbacks, renamed callbacks occupying matching slots, group scheduling callbacks when enabled, and trailing private area, with the compartment form ending exactly at that private area so later processor only fields are never accessed for compartment form.

Idle subsystem initialization registers idle and processor selection helper sets across structure operation, tracing and system call program flavors, chaining attempts so that the initial failure outcome determines the result.
Idle processor tracking record holds a pair of variable sized processor sets, one capturing fully idle processors and the other capturing simultaneous multithreading related idleness.

Masked selection argument record carries prior processor, wakeup attributes and selection modifiers, while task reference and allowed set travel as separate parameters because reference semantics do not compose.
Four jump label switches govern built in idle tracking, per node tracking, and topology awareness for last level cache and non uniform memory domains, all starting in the disabled state.

Global idle state lives in a single static record, per node state in a table addressed by node, per processor scratch views for local, cache and node scopes, plus per processor unvisited node sets supporting search.

Node validation requires per node tracking to be active, treats the absent node marker as not found without critical error, rejects out of range or impossible nodes as invalid with scheduler diagnostic, and otherwise echoes the supplied node.
Enabled check reports whether built in idle tracking is active and emits a scheduler diagnostic when it is disabled.

Selection path uses caller held task protection when inside the processor selection callback after confirming the task matches the recorded wakeup task, requires the target to be queued on the currently locked request queue when another operation holds that lock and otherwise refuses foreign tasks, and otherwise acquires the task lock while preserving interrupt state.

Tasks bound to a single processor or with migration disabled bypass general selection and succeed only when the prior processor remains allowed and can be atomically claimed from idle state, otherwise reporting busy.

Migration disabled evaluation treats a single disable reference specially under preemptible read copy update by comparing the target against current execution context, and otherwise follows the truth of the disable counter.

Default selection helper resolves the scheduler from program context under read copy update protection, delegates to shared selection with default affinity and no extra modifiers, signals idle success through an out parameter, and falls back to the prior processor when no idle processor is available.

Masked selection helpers accept an explicit allowed set with either packed arguments or flat arguments, resolve the scheduler from program context or from the global root, refuse service when subordinate schedulers are attached because caller attribution would be ambiguous, and otherwise delegate to shared selection.

Node scoped and global mask getters resolve the scheduler under read copy update protection, enforce mode compatibility, return the empty set on missing scheduler, disabled tracking or mode mismatch, and otherwise expose read only idle or multithreading masks, while the put helper is intentionally empty and exists only to confer trusted pointer semantics.
Processor to node mapping validates scheduler and processor under read copy update protection and returns the absent marker when validation fails.

Idle test and clear atomically claims a processor when tracking is active and the processor is valid, idle picking returns an idle processor or an error, and arbitrary picking falls back to distributed choice inside the node or globally when no idle processor exists.

Global mask and picking interfaces are forbidden while per node tracking is active and report scheduler diagnostics, whereas node scoped variants depend on shared node validation which itself requires per node tracking.
Two descriptors bind helper identity tables for idle and processor selection families to common ownership and a shared context filter.
Dispatch verdict enumeration distinguishes empty, local queue ready, retain prior task, and retry selection for pick helpers.
Extension headers use conventional include guards to ensure single inclusion.

Foreign task selection while a request queue lock is held is refused with scheduler diagnostic, selection with subordinate schedulers attached is rejected due to ambiguous attribution, and returned masks are global read only views that callers must not mutate.

Initialization advances through layout validation, helper registration, idle setup, operation registration, notification attachment and filesystem object creation, halting with diagnostic upon the initial failure without showing unwind of earlier steps.

Most helpers run under read copy update protection while resolving scheduler state and consulting idle state, with extra task locking confined to the selection path when no outer lock is already held.
Scheduler exposes processor selection, node lookup, idle mask access, idle test and clear, and idle or arbitrary processor picking as callable helpers for BPF programs subject to context filtering.
